_comment: The gateway's own tools AND the house's MCP tools, as the builder offers
them. What each MCP tool DOES still comes live from script-runner's /mcp
(tools/list); what it is ALLOWED to do is decided here, because that is a policy and policies are not read off the thing they govern.
Why a list in the repo, against the plan's preference for asking the
gateway: the gateway has no command that lists its tool ids together
with what each can DO, and the second half is what a person deciding
an agent's rights needs. A checkbox labelled `exec` says nothing; one
labelled 'runs shell commands in the container' is a decision.
`risk`: read = harmless to the machine, write = changes files in the
agent's workspace, act = reaches beyond the workspace or beyond the
house. The tool bench of 2026-09-01 measured models reaching for exec,
edit, cron and sub-agents to get past a locked gate -- every one of
those is `act` here, and the builder paints them red.
Drift against the gateway is caught at rollout: `config patch`
validates tool ids, so a stale entry here fails loudly, not quietly.

`mcp` classifies the house's own MCP tools by their bare name, the same read/write/act scale. A name that is not listed counts as `act`: an unknown tool is the widest one, not the narrowest (ADR-029). A test pins this list against the tools mcp_tools.py actually defines, so a rename fails a suite instead of silently reclassifying a tool.

tools.what: Fetches one memory note by id. Read-only.
Searches the gateway's memory notes. Read-only.
Reads files in the agent's own workspace: its method, a briefing handed to it, its skills.
Reports the agent's own session: model, context used, tokens. Harmless.
Applies a diff to workspace files. Measured in the tool bench as a route around a lock.
Patches files in place. Measured being used to rewrite the rule that forbade opening a gate.
Creates and edits skills. Measured rewriting the very rule that forbade opening a gate.
Creates or overwrites files in the workspace. An agent with this can rewrite its own rules.
Drives a browser from the gateway. Reaches the web and leaves traces there.
Schedules future runs. An agent that can schedule itself outlives the conversation.
Runs shell commands inside the gateway container, sandbox off. The tool models reach for first to get around a lock.
The embedded pipeline runner. DOES NOT hold at input gates and resolves approvals itself -- never grant this; use mora02__flow_run.
Sends messages on the connected channels (Signal). Reaches phones.
Manages background processes started with exec. Only meaningful with exec.
Sends a message into another agent's session. Measured as a route around a lock.
Starts a sub-agent. Measured as a route around a lock: the child had the tools the parent lacked.
Fetches a URL from the gateway itself. Prefer the house's mora02__web_read, which records what was fetched.
The gateway's own search, via an external provider. Prefer mora02__web_search, which stays on the local engine.
